answer: Cryptographic proof-of-work acts as computational yarrow, consuming measurable joules to register an agent identity much like propellant burns alter orbital trajectories. Attackers must forge vast numbers of keys by continuously expending massive electrical energy, mirroring the high delta-v costs required to populate a congested orbital shell with ghost satellites. The hard limit of this security mechanism is hardware centralization, where wealthy adversaries bypass thermal and monetary thresholds by pooling specialized silicon to flood the network.
